LLM_description:
Situation:
A complex emergency has disrupted the main road network across the central river corridor. Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Hub Delta remain operational with limited stocks and staging capacity. Forward Operating Base Alpha, Field Hospital Echo, and Relief Battalion Sierra require immediate resupply of priority lifesaving items and shelter commodities. Several arterial routes are degraded by washouts, unstable bridges, and sporadic security incidents. Airlift is constrained, placing the bulk of the distribution burden on protected road convoys.

Mission:
Deliver essential supplies from rear depots to forward units during the current operational period while minimizing total operational cost, maintaining force protection standards, and ensuring the highest possible service level to critical sites.

Execution/Concept:
- Origin-to-destination movements will be ground convoys from Supply Depot Bravo and Logistics Hub Delta to assigned forward units. Dispatch plans must respect depot stock limits; no location will issue more than it holds for any item.
- Each forward unit’s requirement must be met through delivered cargo and, if necessary, an explicitly tolerated shortfall. Any unmet portion will be recorded as a shortfall and will incur penalty costs representing humanitarian impact and follow-on response burdens.
- Vehicles are standardized and tracked by corridor. Total loaded volume per convoy leg cannot exceed per-vehicle capacity multiplied by the number of vehicles assigned on that leg. Per-item packing factors determine how much of each item can be carried per vehicle.
- A corridor is considered active only if at least one vehicle is dispatched on that origin-to-destination leg during the period. Activating a corridor triggers a fixed Risk Cost for security overhead (escort teams, route clearance, and coordination) that is incurred once per corridor regardless of the number of vehicles sent. Vehicles may only operate on corridors that have been activated.
- The aggregate number of vehicles deployed across all corridors will not exceed the available fleet. Each vehicle dispatched carries a per-vehicle operating cost accounting for crews, fuel, and maintenance.
- Transport costs reflect distance, terrain, and time for each origin-destination pair. The planning objective is to allocate flows, decide which corridors to activate, and assign vehicles such that the sum of transport costs, fixed route Risk Costs, vehicle deployment costs, and shortage penalties is minimized.
- Prioritization: Medical stabilization sites and high-density shelters have priority for water, medical, and shelter materials. Where routes are insecure or capacity-limited, planners may deliberately accept controlled shortfalls if the combined penalty and future re-supply posture is preferable to activating additional high-risk corridors.
